# Requirements Document

## Introduction

This spec covers **one diagram type, `w3c/owl`** — an OWL 2 ontology, read from the same Turtle/N-Triples bytes the family's engine parses, drawn as the schema it asserts: classes, properties, individuals, and the axioms relating them. It is the first sibling of the anchor spec [`rdf-diagram`](../rdf-diagram/requirements.md), consumes that spec's shared machinery by name, and restates none of it — a rule appearing in both documents means one of the two is wrong.

| Origin | File visualized | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `w3c/owl` | A Turtle (`.ttl`) or N-Triples (`.nt`) file carrying an ontology | The TBox as a graph: classes and their hierarchy, properties with domains and ranges, restrictions, set operators, equivalence and disjointness — plus the individuals the file asserts |

**The format, as researched.** OWL 2 (W3C recommendation, second edition 2012) is an ontology language layered on RDF: in the mapping to RDF graphs, a class is an IRI typed `owl:Class`, object and datatype properties are IRIs typed `owl:ObjectProperty`/`owl:DatatypeProperty`, hierarchy is `rdfs:subClassOf`/`rdfs:subPropertyOf`, and the axioms this reading draws are triples — `owl:equivalentClass`, `owl:disjointWith`, `rdfs:domain`/`rdfs:range`, property characteristics as types (`owl:FunctionalProperty`, `owl:TransitiveProperty`, …), `owl:inverseOf`. **Class expressions are blank-node structures**: a restriction is `[ a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty :p ; owl:someValuesFrom :C ]`, and unions, intersections and complements are blank nodes over `rdf:List`s. An ontology declares itself with an `owl:Ontology` header and may state `owl:imports`. Individuals are ABox triples in the same file. Sources are listed at the end.

## Shared machinery consumed, by name

From `rdf-diagram`: the **triplestore document store** (this spec adds a projection over its model, never a parser), the **serialization boundary**, the **splice discipline** (this reading's gestures are its triple-writer under OWL names), the **blank-node identity boundary**, the **drawn-element budget** (measured against this reading's projection), the **layout overlay**, the **routing arrangement** (this reading never claims a bare body and is Add-suggested off its `owl:Ontology` marker), the **no-network, no-inference rule**, and the **example vendoring rule**.

## How OWL ontologies are visualized — research, and the positions taken

OWL has the strongest visualization tradition of the four family readings, and one named convention: **VOWL, the Visual Notation for OWL Ontologies** (Lohmann, Negru, Haag, Ertl — Semantic Web Journal 2016; VOWL 2 specification). What VOWL specifies: classes as labeled circles and datatypes as bordered rectangles; `rdfs:subClassOf` as a dotted edge labeled "Subclass of"; object properties as directed edges wearing borderless label rectangles, datatype properties as labeled edges to datatype rectangles; equivalence as a doubled circle border carrying both names; disjointness as a dedicated edge symbol; set operators as circles carrying ∪/∩/¬; cardinality restrictions as annotations on the property edge; property characteristics as words in the property label; `owl:Thing` as a small dashed circle that also anchors domain-less properties; external/imported and deprecated elements dimmed. Its reference implementations are **WebVOWL** and the **ProtégéVOWL** plugin. Where practitioners find it wanting is equally documented: the prescribed **force-directed layout** is non-deterministic and turns mid-sized ontologies into hairballs; deeply **nested class expressions** (a restriction whose filler is a union of restrictions) outgrow edge annotations; and the ABox is a stated afterthought — VOWL 2's own scope is the schema. The other traditions confirm the split: **Protégé**, the field's default editor, shows the everyday view as an indented, asserted **class tree**, not a graph; **OWLGrEd** and **Graffoo** map OWL onto UML-class-diagram conventions for publication figures. A domain note recorded so nobody retraces it: the VOWL specification's historical home, `vowl.visualdataweb.org`, now redirects to an unrelated site — the notation's citable sources are the journal paper and the WebVOWL deployments, and the catalog row is updated accordingly by this spec.

**Adopted, with reasons.**

- **VOWL's structural vocabulary**: circle classes, rectangle datatypes, dotted subclass edges, labeled property edges, doubled border for equivalence, set-operator nodes, characteristics as words in the label, dimmed external and deprecated elements, `owl:Thing` anchoring domain-less properties. It is the one notation in this family with a written specification and multiple implementations — exactly the "don't reinvent" case — and its primitives map one-to-one onto the central canvas library's elements and connections.
- **Datatypes as nodes** — VOWL's convention, and the half of the literal-node question the anchor left "the OWL sibling's tradition to weigh": in an ontology the datatype **is** the structure being communicated (`:birthDate` ranging over `xsd:date` is the point of the axiom), so a datatype property draws as an edge to a datatype rectangle. The anchor's rejection stands for **data volume**: an individual's literal assertions draw as property rows inside the individual's card, per the family's card convention — datatype nodes for schema, literal rows for data, each where its tradition is right.
- **The asserted class tree as a second lens**: Protégé's everyday view earns a place — the deterministic computed layout arranges the class graph by its asserted `rdfs:subClassOf` depth (roots left, leaves right), so the graph reads as the tree a Protégé user expects without a second view mechanism.

**Rejected, with reasons.**

- **Force-directed layout** — VOWL's prescription, rejected already by the anchor for the whole family: non-deterministic layouts break the same-file-opens-the-same-way rule and the layout overlay both. VOWL's *vocabulary* survives without its *physics*.
- **VOWL's fixed color palette** — the notation's blues and greens are an identity, not a semantics; this module distinguishes element kinds through the canvas library's theme-aware styling, keeping shape and edge-style as the load-bearing distinctions.
- **Inline rendering of arbitrarily nested class expressions** — the documented place VOWL outgrows itself. Nesting is bounded honestly (Requirement 3.4) instead of drawing an unreadable thicket.
- **UML-notation mapping (OWLGrEd/Graffoo)** — a publication-figure tradition; adopting two notations at once would serve neither.

## Alignment with Product Vision

- [product.md](../../steering/product.md)'s **"Don't reinvent, integrate"** — OWL 2 is a W3C recommendation and VOWL a published notation with implementations; this spec adopts both by citation and adds no format and no notation of its own.
- product.md's **"Files are the source of truth"** and **"Linkage over illustration"** — the diagram renders the ontology file the repository already has; every element is a term in that file; edits are reviewable splices and positions live in the `.adp` overlay.
- [tech.md](../../steering/tech.md)'s **Diagram storage**, **Commands**, and [structure.md](../../steering/structure.md)'s **dependency direction** — inherited through the anchor's machinery; this reading is a further `DiagramDefinition` inside `src/diagrams/rdf/`, the C4/databricks multi-definition arrangement, so the family stays one engine and **no new module folder is created**.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — The projection: which triples become which elements

**User Story:** As an ontology author, I want the diagram built from OWL's own vocabulary rather than raw triples, so that a class reads as a class and not as a node that happens to have a type.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the reading projects the parsed model THEN every IRI declared or used as a class (`owl:Class`, or the object of `rdfs:subClassOf`/`rdfs:domain`/`rdfs:range`) SHALL become a class node; every `owl:ObjectProperty` a property edge between its stated domain and range classes; every `owl:DatatypeProperty` a property edge from its domain class to a datatype node; and `owl:Thing` SHALL be drawn only where the file states it or a domain-less/range-less property needs its VOWL anchor.
2. WHEN a property states no domain or range THEN the missing end SHALL anchor at `owl:Thing` per the adopted convention, visually distinct from a stated `owl:Thing` axiom.
3. WHEN individuals appear (`owl:NamedIndividual`, or an IRI typed by a class of this ontology) THEN each SHALL draw as a card bearing its types as badges and its literal assertions as property rows — the family card convention — with object-property assertions between individuals as edges.
4. WHEN annotation assertions appear (`rdfs:label`, `rdfs:comment`, `owl:versionInfo`, …) THEN they SHALL populate the element's property rows and the property grid, and `rdfs:label` SHALL be the preferred display name with the prefixed name as fallback.
5. WHEN the `owl:Ontology` header is present THEN it SHALL draw as one header element carrying the ontology IRI and its annotations, and each `owl:imports` SHALL show as a row on it — imported, per the **no-network, no-inference rule**, meaning *named, never fetched*.
6. WHEN entities are deprecated (`owl:deprecated true`) or external (an IRI outside the ontology's own namespace, used but not declared here) THEN they SHALL draw dimmed per the adopted convention, so the reader sees what this file owns versus what it borrows.

### Requirement 2 — Axioms as edges: hierarchy, equivalence, disjointness

**User Story:** As a reader, I want the axioms that give an ontology its shape drawn in the notation their tradition uses, so that a subclass edge is recognizably not an object property.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN `rdfs:subClassOf` relates two named classes THEN it SHALL draw as VOWL's dotted subclass edge, and the deterministic computed layout SHALL arrange class nodes by asserted subclass depth — the Protégé-tree lens — so the same file always opens the same way.
2. WHEN `owl:equivalentClass` relates two named classes THEN the adopted doubled-border convention SHALL apply, both names legible; WHEN `owl:disjointWith` (or an `owl:AllDisjointClasses` group) is asserted THEN it SHALL draw as the dedicated disjointness edge or group marker.
3. WHEN `rdfs:subPropertyOf`, `owl:inverseOf`, or property characteristics (`owl:FunctionalProperty`, `owl:InverseFunctionalProperty`, `owl:TransitiveProperty`, `owl:SymmetricProperty`, …) are asserted THEN they SHALL appear as the property label's characteristic words and inverse pairing per VOWL, not as invented extra nodes.
4. WHEN the same IRI is punned (OWL 2 permits one IRI as both class and individual) THEN each role SHALL draw in its own projection place, and the property grid SHALL name the punning rather than either role silently winning.

### Requirement 3 — Restrictions and class expressions: the blank-node intersection

**User Story:** As an ontology author whose classes are defined by restrictions, I want those structures visible on the diagram, so that `Vegetarian ⊑ ∀hasTopping.VegetarianTopping` is readable without opening the Turtle — while the tool stays honest about what an anonymous structure can and cannot do.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a class expression appears (an `owl:Restriction`; an `owl:unionOf`/`owl:intersectionOf`/`owl:complementOf` structure) THEN it SHALL draw as a compact expression node in the adopted vocabulary — quantifier or cardinality plus property for restrictions (`∃ hasTopping`, `= 1 hasBase`, `∀ hasTopping`), the set-operator symbol for combinations — connected to the named class that uses it and to the named classes and datatypes it references.
2. BECAUSE such structures are blank-node-rooted, the **blank-node identity boundary** applies whole: expression nodes SHALL take their computed place beside the class that uses them, SHALL refuse stored positions, and SHALL refuse canvas edits — with the boundary's reason stated wherever the refusal surfaces. Editing a class expression is text-editor work in this version, and the spec says so rather than promising otherwise.
3. WHEN the file's `rdf:List` plumbing underlies a union or intersection THEN the cons-pairs SHALL stay in the file, never on the canvas, per the family's collection rendering.
4. WHEN expressions nest beyond **two levels** THEN deeper levels SHALL render as an elided expression node labeled with a summary (`…`, expandable in the property grid's read-only text), because inline rendering of arbitrary nesting is the documented place the tradition fails; the elision SHALL be visible as such, never silent.
5. WHEN a restriction structure is malformed (an `owl:Restriction` without `owl:onProperty`, an `owl:unionOf` whose list is broken) THEN the element SHALL draw as a marked problem node and validation SHALL report it (Requirement 5), the file still opening per the family's degrade-don't-refuse stance.

### Requirement 4 — Asserted only: what no-inference means for an ontology

**User Story:** As a user who knows OWL, I want to be told plainly that this diagram is the asserted ontology, so that I never mistake the drawn hierarchy for the inferred one a reasoner would show me.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the diagram draws THEN it SHALL show exactly what the file asserts — the **no-network, no-inference rule**, which lands harder here than anywhere else in the family: an OWL user's daily tools (Protégé with a reasoner attached) show an *inferred* hierarchy, and this diagram deliberately does not. No subsumption is computed, no equivalence is propagated, no domain/range is used to type anything, no individual is classified, and a class asserted under two parents shows exactly two subclass edges.
2. WHEN the ontology states `owl:imports` THEN validation SHALL carry one info naming the imports and stating that they are not fetched, so a reader knows the drawn ontology is this file alone rather than its import closure.
3. WHEN this reading is documented — its definition description, its catalog row — THEN the asserted-not-inferred stance SHALL be stated in the reader's terms ("shows what the file says; a reasoner would show more").

### Requirement 5 — Validation: structural facts about the asserted ontology

**User Story:** As an author, I want the problems panel to catch what makes an ontology structurally wrong or misleading as text, without a reasoner's opinions arriving uninvited.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the asserted `rdfs:subClassOf` graph over named classes contains a cycle THEN validation SHALL report it as a warning naming the cycle's classes — a cycle is legal OWL (it asserts mutual equivalence) and is almost always an authoring mistake, which is exactly what a warning is for.
2. WHEN a malformed class expression appears (Requirement 3.5) THEN validation SHALL report it as an error with the line.
3. WHEN an IRI is used as a property in axiom positions (`rdfs:domain`, `owl:onProperty`) but declared nowhere in the file THEN validation SHALL report an info naming it — often an import-resident term, which the no-fetch stance makes worth surfacing rather than an error.
4. WHEN a deprecated entity is referenced by a non-deprecated axiom THEN validation SHALL report an info.
5. WHEN validation runs THEN it SHALL be a pure function over this reading's projection, consulting nothing outside the file, and SHALL NOT restate the anchor's file-level rules (parse errors, prefix redeclarations) — those arrive from the shared engine.

### Requirement 6 — Editing: the ontology gestures, as splices

**User Story:** As an author, I want the edits a schema canvas is good at — a subclass edge, a new class, a rename, a label — landing in my Turtle as minimal reviewable diffs, each one undo away.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a subclass edge is drawn between two named classes THEN one `rdfs:subClassOf` triple SHALL be spliced per the **splice discipline**, with a byte-restoring inverse; drawing one that already exists SHALL be refused with the reason.
2. WHEN a class is created (toolbox drop) THEN it SHALL be written as an IRI with one `a owl:Class` triple, named through the family's prefix-validated dialog; object and datatype properties SHALL be creatable the same way with their type triple, and stating a domain or range SHALL be its own gesture splicing its own triple.
3. WHEN a term is renamed, or removed with its references THEN the family's rename/remove commands SHALL apply as-is under this reading's names, counts stated before anything runs.
4. WHEN `rdfs:label` or `rdfs:comment` is edited through the property grid THEN the edit SHALL land through the standard property path as a splice on that annotation triple.
5. IF a gesture targets a class expression, any blank-node-rooted structure, a truncated view, or an unregistered bare file THEN it SHALL be refused before any splice with the governing boundary's sentence (**blank-node identity boundary**, **drawn-element budget**, **layout overlay**).

### Requirement 7 — Toolbox, context actions, property grid

**User Story:** As a user, I want the palette and panels to speak OWL — class, object property, datatype property, individual — through the standard provider paths.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the diagram is open THEN the toolbox SHALL offer Class, Object property, Datatype property and Individual (each dropped via placement id and written per Requirement 6.2); there SHALL be no restriction entry, because a restriction needs a structure no drop can state — the same reasoning the wardley-map spec recorded for links, stated here for expressions.
2. WHEN a class is selected THEN the property grid SHALL show its IRI (read-only, rename as the identity path), label and comment (editable), its asserted superclasses, equivalents and disjoints, and the expressions defining it as read-only text in Manchester-style rendering (`∃ hasTopping.Cheese`), with the blank-node boundary as the stated reason.
3. WHEN a property element is selected THEN the grid SHALL show its characteristics, domain, range and inverse; WHEN an individual is selected, its types and assertions — every unavailable edit carrying its reason per the family's discovery rule.

### Requirement 8 — Registration, routing and scale

**User Story:** As a user, I want opening an ontology as an ontology to be a deliberate, suggested choice that never hijacks the plain graph reading, and to degrade honestly on large ontologies.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module declares this reading THEN it SHALL be a further `DiagramDefinition` (`w3c/owl`, description carrying the asserted-not-inferred stance, fitting icon) inside `src/diagrams/rdf/` over the shared store — no new module folder, per the family arrangement.
2. WHEN a bare `.ttl`/`.nt` opens THEN it SHALL route to `w3c/rdf` per the **routing arrangement**; this reading SHALL be chosen by explicit registration, and Add SHALL suggest it when the file carries the `owl:Ontology` marker triple.
3. WHEN the projection exceeds the **drawn-element budget** THEN the truncated view, banner and withheld edits SHALL apply as the anchor defines them, measured against this reading's projected elements — and truncation order SHALL keep whole class neighborhoods together (a class with its expressions) rather than splitting them mid-structure.
4. WHEN several registrations read one file THEN this reading SHALL share the one parsed document, edits visible across all readings, one history.

### Requirement 9 — Examples: real ontologies, vendored honestly

**User Story:** As a user meeting the ontology reading, I want real published ontologies — the ones the field actually teaches and ships — opening from the explorer, so the diagram proves itself on the tradition's own corpus.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the reading ships THEN its examples SHALL be vendored under the **example vendoring rule**, each license verified individually at acquisition. Candidates verified during this spec's research: **PROV-O** (the W3C provenance ontology, `w3.org/ns/prov`, W3C Software and Document License; ~30 classes with restrictions and characteristics — the mid-size real-standard example), **OWL-Time or the Organization ontology** (W3C-licensed, natively published as Turtle — a second W3C vocabulary exercising domains/ranges and individuals), and the **pizza ontology** (`owlcs/pizza-ontology`, verified CC BY 3.0 — attribution carried per the vendoring rule; the field's canonical teaching ontology and the restriction showcase Requirement 3 needs). A budget-exceeding candidate — a large CC BY 4.0 OBO ontology such as the Gene Ontology — MAY be vendored as an extract to demonstrate truncation on a real ontology. Substitution at acquisition time is allowed under the same verification.
2. WHEN an upstream ontology is published only in RDF/XML (pizza, most OBO releases) THEN vendoring it requires conversion to Turtle, and the conversion SHALL be recorded in the provenance readme as exactly the local change it is, tool and version named — the **serialization boundary** makes this unavoidable and the vendoring rule makes it honest.
3. WHEN the examples ship THEN at least one SHALL exercise restrictions, set operators and deep nesting (Requirement 3 demonstrated on real axioms), at least one SHALL carry individuals alongside its TBox, and each SHALL open with zero validation findings above info level; replication into `src/examples/` follows the central rule by construction.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- This reading is **a projection, a layout lens, a validator, writers for its gestures, and a definition** inside `src/diagrams/rdf/` — pure functions over the anchor's parsed model wherever no file I/O is inherent. It owns no parser, no store, no serialization code.
- Element ids for named terms are the family's IRI-derived ids; expression nodes take deterministic structural ids that the **blank-node identity boundary** governs.

### Performance

- Projection linear in triple count; everything drawn is bounded by the **drawn-element budget**. The Manchester-style expression rendering is computed per selected element, not for the whole file.

### Security

- The **no-network, no-inference rule**, inherited whole — `owl:imports` is the family's named no-fetch case and this reading's most tempting violation; Requirement 4.2 makes the refusal visible instead of silent.

### Reliability

- Round-trip byte-identity is the anchor store's guarantee; this spec adds fixture coverage for the constructs its projection reads (restrictions, set-operator lists, punning, deprecation, the ontology header) so a projection change cannot silently misread an axiom shape.
- Every refusal this spec names (expression edits, restriction repositioning, truncation, unregistered bare file) carries its sentence in a test.

### Usability

- Labels preferred, prefixed names as fallback, full IRIs one selection away; the asserted-not-inferred stance stated where a reader will actually see it (definition description, import info, catalog row).

## Sources

- OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Overview (Second Edition) — w3.org/TR/owl2-overview
- OWL 2 Mapping to RDF Graphs — w3.org/TR/owl2-mapping-to-rdf (restrictions and expressions as blank-node structures)
- VOWL: Visualizing Ontologies with VOWL — Lohmann, Negru, Haag, Ertl, Semantic Web Journal 2016 (semantic-web-journal.net/system/files/swj750.pdf); the specification's historical domain `vowl.visualdataweb.org` has lapsed to an unrelated site, verified during this research
- WebVOWL deployment — service.tib.eu/webvowl (the notation's reference implementation)
- ProtégéVOWL — Lohmann et al., ISWC 2014 (the Protégé-plugin implementation); Protégé itself for the asserted class-tree lens
- OWLGrEd (owlgred.lumii.lv) and Graffoo (essepuntato.it/graffoo) — the UML-mapping tradition, considered and not adopted
- PROV-O: The PROV Ontology — w3.org/TR/prov-o (W3C license; OWL-RL-profile-conformant but drawn asserted-only here)
- Pizza ontology — github.com/owlcs/pizza-ontology (verified CC BY 3.0; attribution carried if vendored)
- OWL-Time — w3.org/TR/owl-time · The Organization Ontology — w3.org/TR/vocab-org (W3C-licensed Turtle-native candidates)
- Gene Ontology — geneontology.org (CC BY 4.0; the budget-exceeding candidate, extract + conversion recorded if used)
